note: A handful of statistical offices publish total fertility by ancestry, immigrant category, mother's country of birth, or religion. Definitions are not comparable across countries. We chart official series only — never estimates pieced together from population shares.

countries.detail: CBS period TFR by religion of the woman (Jewish, Muslim, Druze, Arab, national), 1960 and 2000–2023. Haredi TFR is not in that religion table; IDI reports 6.4 in 2020–2022 versus 2.5 for other Jewish women.
IIPS / MoHFW National Family Health Survey — TFR (ages 15–49) by religion, NFHS-1 (1992–93) through NFHS-5 (2019–21). Table 4.2 in NFHS-5. Not an annual vital-statistics series.

NIPS / PDHS fertility tables (including 2017–18 Table 5.2) split TFR by residence, education, wealth, and province — not by religion. The Pakistan census publishes population by religion, not TFR. Pakistan is ~96% Muslim, so a religion-disaggregated TFR comparable to India’s NFHS Table 4.2 is not in the official reports.
Statistics Denmark FERT1 — TFR (ages 15–49) for Danish origin, western/non-western immigrants, and western/non-western descendants, 1986–2025.

Statistics Norway table 12482 — TFR by mother's immigrant category (immigrants, Norwegian-born to immigrant parents, other population), 2011–2025. Table 12481 further splits immigrant women by region of origin.
CBS published TFR by migration background; the classification was retired in favour of a country-of-origin system, so there is no continuous public series in the old categories.
Statistics Sweden publishes fertility by mother's country of birth in demographic reports; not a single FERT1-style ancestry time series in the same western/non-western split.
ONS publishes TFR in England and Wales by mother's country of birth (UK-born vs non-UK-born, plus selected countries). That is nativity, not DST ancestry.
NCHS publishes TFR by race and Hispanic origin of the mother (not immigrant ancestry). birthrate.io charts the 1980–2026 compilation on /fertility/race; 2024–2026 are provisional.
Statistik Austria TFR by Austrian vs foreign origin (with EU/EFTA/UK, former Yugoslavia, Turkey, elsewhere), including Vienna splits. 2025 national TFR 1.30 is the lowest on record.
Kosovo MICS rounds publish TFR for Albanian and Roma/Ashkali/Egyptian communities. Not a vital-registration ancestry series; Serb TFR was suppressed for sample size in the newest round.
Destatis publishes live births by mother's citizenship. A continuous TFR by migration background comparable to FERT1 is not on the open tables.
INED/INSEE analyse fertility by parents' place of birth in reports. France does not publish a DST-style annual ancestry TFR table.
Statistics Finland publishes some fertility figures by origin in demographic reviews, not a full open ancestry TFR series like FERT1.
Statistics Canada has estimated TFR by immigrant status in analytical papers; not a continuous StatBank-style ancestry table.
